steps.label: capture root container pre-probe (banked for the closing machine diff)
steps.expect: zero exit; capture the root listing as the blast-radius reference AND bank it to /run/vdpsw2-pre.census (board-local tmpfs, so a reboot clears it) — the closing census (last step) machine-diffs the fresh listing against that banked reference for zero deltas. dpsw-typestate task 6.2 discovery sitting (bead dpaa2-controlplane-dbf.16), amended to revision 2 after the V-DPSW-2-run1 teardown divergence (bead dpaa2-controlplane-dbf.18). ADR-0003 §5 queries are lifecycle-only. This plan names no dpmac and nothing in the ADR-0003 §4 total-deny set — every bind runs on objects this plan itself creates, never on standing topology (design D9; DPRC-I6).

steps.label: create + label scratch child dprc as vdpsw2
cmd: set -e; n=$(restool --script dprc create dprc.1); restool dprc set-label "$n" --label=vdpsw2; echo "created $n labelled vdpsw2"
steps.expect: zero exit; the child is created then labelled in one shell step, capturing the pool-assigned name from create stdout (the sanctioned sh -c use, V-DPRC-10). Objects live in the scratch child where containable (design D9); the FDB create-visible shape (step d1) lands here so DPRC-I6 keeps it off the fsl-mc bus and no kernel driver probes it. The bind probes (reset scope, bpid, FDB bind outcome) need the kernel to bind, so they run at ROOT on objects this plan creates — never on standing topology (design D9; DPRC-I6: child residents never reach the bus). Label-scoped teardown below.

steps.label: DPSW-I3/I9 defer face: create the bindable reference dpsw + its dpmcp at root, WITHOUT a dpbp
cmd: set -e; m=$(restool --script dpmcp create --container=dprc.1); restool dprc set-label "$m" --label=vdpsw2mcp1; s=$(restool --script dpsw create --num-ifs=2 --flooding-cfg=DPSW_FLOODING_PER_FDB --broadcast-cfg=DPSW_BROADCAST_PER_FDB --container=dprc.1); restool dprc set-label "$s" --label=vdpsw2sw1; restool dprc assign dprc.1 --object="$m" --plugged=1; restool dprc assign dprc.1 --object="$s" --plugged=1; restool dprc sync; echo "created+plugged dpmcp=$m dpsw=$s (no dpbp companion yet; no ports connected)"
steps.expect: zero exit; the kernel-bindable shape (ctrl-if on by default, flooding+broadcast PER_FDB, DPSW-I1) built at ROOT with its dpmcp companion but deliberately WITHOUT a dpbp companion, so the probe has no companion dpbp to draw (DPSW-I9). No ports are connected — the switch binds on its object + companions alone, touching no standing dpmac (design D9). The defer-vs-bind judgment is the next step. Both objects are labelled for the label-scoped teardown.

steps.label: DPSW-I3/I9: pre-bind dpsw info (reset-scope BEFORE) + bounded settle — expect SILENT defer, not a failure
cmd: s=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | awk '$2=="vdpsw2sw1"{print $1; exit}'); [ -n "$s" ] || { echo 'no vdpsw2sw1 resolved' >&2; exit 1; }; restool dpsw info "$s"; p="/sys/bus/fsl-mc/devices/$s/driver"; i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 10 ]; do readlink "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; i=$((i+1)); done; echo "$s" > /sys/bus/fsl-mc/drivers_probe 2>/dev/null || true; i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 5 ]; do readlink "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; i=$((i+1)); done; restool dprc sync 1>&2 || true; i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 10 ]; do readlink "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; i=$((i+1)); done; if readlink "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "RESULT: BOUND — the switch bound WITHOUT a created dpbp companion (finding: a root-pool dpbp satisfied the probe draw)"; else echo "RESULT: DEFERRED — no driver link after the bounded settle"; fi; dmesg 2>/dev/null | tail -40 | grep -iE 'dpsw|EOPNOTSUPP|cannot probe' || echo "(no dpsw probe-error line in recent dmesg — a silent defer, not a failure)"
steps.expect: any exit — the finding is in the output, not the status (DPSW-I7). EXPECTED: the dpaa2-switch probe DEFERS SILENTLY — no driver link after the bind_settle discipline (bounded poll + drivers_probe kick + dprc sync kick, the generate.rs bind_settle semantics), and NO -EOPNOTSUPP / 'cannot probe' line in dmesg. That distinguishes 'silently deferred' (DPSW-I9 defer-not-fail: the missing companion stalls the probe, it does not fail) from 'failed' (a loud driver refusal). If it BOUND, the finding is that a root-pool dpbp satisfied the draw (the DPSW-I3 live-defer face, unprobed until now). The dpsw info output above is the reset-scope BEFORE snapshot for the DPSW-I4 after/before compare (step b).

steps.label: DPSW-I9: create the dpbp companion, kick the bus, and the bind completes (defer-not-fail)
cmd: s=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | awk '$2=="vdpsw2sw1"{print $1; exit}'); [ -n "$s" ] || { echo 'no vdpsw2sw1 resolved' >&2; exit 1; }; b=$(restool --script dpbp create --container=dprc.1); restool dprc set-label "$b" --label=vdpsw2bp1; restool dprc assign dprc.1 --object="$b" --plugged=1; echo "$s" > /sys/bus/fsl-mc/drivers_probe 2>/dev/null || true; restool dprc sync 1>&2 || true; p="/sys/bus/fsl-mc/devices/$s/driver"; i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 10 ]; do readlink "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; i=$((i+1)); done; if readlink "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "RESULT: BOUND after adding the dpbp + kick — the defer resolved, not a failure (DPSW-I9)"; else echo "RESULT: STILL DEFERRED after dpbp + kick (finding)"; fi
steps.expect: any exit; EXPECTED: adding the missing dpbp companion in the dpsw's own container and kicking the bus (drivers_probe + dprc sync, the bind_settle kicks) completes the bind — the deferred probe was waiting on the companion, never failing (DPSW-I9 defer-not-fail, grounding the DPSW-I3 defer face). A still-deferred result is the finding. One settle per judgment, the bind_settle discipline (design D10; V-TRAF-1 rev 3).

steps.label: DPSW-I4 reset scope: post-bind dpsw info (reset-scope AFTER) — the evidence is what survived the bind
cmd: s=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | awk '$2=="vdpsw2sw1"{print $1; exit}'); [ -n "$s" ] || { echo 'no vdpsw2sw1 resolved' >&2; exit 1; }; restool dpsw info "$s"
steps.expect: any exit; the post-bind dpsw info, diffed offline against step 4's BEFORE snapshot — the evidence is what survived the bind. REACH LIMIT recorded, not faked (design D9): restool's dpsw verb surface is five verbs (info / create / destroy / update, plus version) with NO reset verb, so dpsw_reset cannot be issued directly — the kernel bind IS the only reset stimulus (bind-resets-object, strong form). And restool dpsw info prints attributes + decoded options + the per-interface block only, NOT the VLAN/FDB tables (docs/baseline/dpsw.md command surface), so the baseline's named defaults (VLAN 1, FDB 0) and their wipe at bind stay UNOBSERVABLE here. DPSW-I4 reset scope is therefore only partly reachable through restool; the model keeps RESET_FACET_SCOPE = ResetTotal (conservative) until the raw-command transport (mc-portal-backend, #10) reads the tables. The attribute block (immutable) is the observable half and should be unchanged across the bind.

steps.label: DPSW-I5 bpid law: dpbp info on the BOUND switch's own dpbp (bpid vs object id)
cmd: b=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | awk '$2=="vdpsw2bp1"{print $1; exit}'); [ -n "$b" ] || { echo 'no vdpsw2bp1 resolved' >&2; exit 1; }; restool dpbp info "$b"; id=$(restool dpbp info "$b" | awk -F': ' '$1=="dpbp id"{print $2; exit}'); bp=$(restool dpbp info "$b" | awk -F': ' '$1=="buffer pool id"{print $2; exit}'); echo "RESULT: dpbp id=${id:-?} buffer pool id=${bp:-?} coincide=$([ "$id" = "$bp" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
steps.expect: any exit; on the BOUND switch's own dpbp (the live switch consumer, extending DPBP-I5 with DPSW-I5), read dpbp id vs buffer pool id (bpid) — the V-READBACK-1 read-back precedent. NOTE: where the two COINCIDE the divergent face stays OPEN — the coincidence is the finding, NOT a proof (DPSW-I5: the in-tree switch datapath uses the object id as bpid and works only where the two happen to coincide; the divergent-id traffic face needs a board where they differ, unavailable here). Record the two ids; do not read a coincidence as the law holding.

steps.label: FDB budget, dpsw.md unknown 6 (create-visible half): a tight split shape in the scratch child (no bind)
cmd: c=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | awk '$2=="vdpsw2"{print $1; exit}'); [ -n "$c" ] || { echo 'no vdpsw2 child resolved' >&2; exit 1; }; s=$(restool --script dpsw create --num-ifs=4 --max-fdbs=4 --max-fdb-entries=4 --flooding-cfg=DPSW_FLOODING_PER_FDB --broadcast-cfg=DPSW_BROADCAST_PER_FDB --container="$c"); restool dprc set-label "$s" --label=vdpsw2fdb; restool dpsw info "$s"; echo "child create-visible: requested num_ifs=4 max_fdbs=4 max_fdb_entries=4 (per-port split 4/4=1); read max_fdb_entries back above"
steps.expect: any exit; the create/bind-VISIBLE half of the FDB budget question (docs/baseline/dpsw.md unknown 6: MC-enforced budget vs driver convention). A lower-bracket shape sized so the per-port split (max_fdb_entries / num_ifs) is exactly 1: read whether the MC keeps max_fdb_entries=4 or clamps it at create. CONTAINED in the scratch child (DPRC-I6, off the bus, no kernel probe) — this half asks only the MC create surface. NOTE: restool cannot add FDB entries (switchdev owns the runtime FDB surface, DPSW-I8), so the runtime budget is unreachable; the plan probes only the create/bind-visible half. The bind-outcome bracket is the next step.

steps.label: FDB budget, dpsw.md unknown 6 (bind-outcome half): a split-violating bindable shape at root — does the kernel enforce?
cmd: set -e; m=$(restool --script dpmcp create --container=dprc.1); restool dprc set-label "$m" --label=vdpsw2mcp2; b=$(restool --script dpbp create --container=dprc.1); restool dprc set-label "$b" --label=vdpsw2bp2; s=$(restool --script dpsw create --num-ifs=4 --max-fdbs=4 --max-fdb-entries=2 --flooding-cfg=DPSW_FLOODING_PER_FDB --broadcast-cfg=DPSW_BROADCAST_PER_FDB --container=dprc.1); restool dprc set-label "$s" --label=vdpsw2sw2; restool dprc assign dprc.1 --object="$m" --plugged=1; restool dprc assign dprc.1 --object="$b" --plugged=1; restool dprc assign dprc.1 --object="$s" --plugged=1; set +e; restool dprc sync; echo "$s" > /sys/bus/fsl-mc/drivers_probe 2>/dev/null || true; p="/sys/bus/fsl-mc/devices/$s/driver"; i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 10 ]; do readlink "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; i=$((i+1)); done; restool dpsw info "$s"; if readlink "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "RESULT: BOUND — kernel accepted per-port split max_fdb_entries(2)/num_ifs(4) < 1 (driver convention, NOT MC-enforced)"; else echo "RESULT: UNBOUND — the split-violating shape did not bind"; fi; dmesg 2>/dev/null | tail -40 | grep -iE 'dpsw|fdb|EOPNOTSUPP|cannot probe' || echo "(no dpsw/fdb line in recent dmesg)"
steps.expect: any exit; the bind-OUTCOME bracket of unknown 6. The upper-bracket shape has max_fdb_entries(2) < num_ifs(4), so the kernel per-port FDB split (max_fdb_entries / num_ifs = 0) would be violated if the budget were MC-enforced. The bind runs on objects this plan creates with its own dpmcp+dpbp companions (design D9), judged via the bind_settle discipline. FINDINGS: a BOUND switch says the split is driver convention (the kernel sized 0 and bound anyway); an UNBOUND switch with an FDB/EOPNOTSUPP dmesg line says it is MC-enforced or kernel-rejected. Record both the dpsw info and the dmesg lines.

steps.label: teardown (label-scoped, judged): allocator-unbind + unplug + destroy every created object; destroy the scratch child; verify no survivor
cmd: set -e; for lbl in vdpsw2sw1 vdpsw2sw2; do o=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | awk -v L="$lbl" '$2==L{print $1; exit}'); [ -n "$o" ] || continue; if [ -e "/sys/bus/fsl-mc/devices/$o/driver" ]; then echo "$o" > "/sys/bus/fsl-mc/devices/$o/driver/unbind"; fi; restool dprc assign dprc.1 --object="$o" --plugged=0 || { echo "FAIL: unplug refused for $o ($lbl)" >&2; exit 1; }; restool dpsw destroy "$o" || { echo "FAIL: destroy refused for $o ($lbl)" >&2; exit 1; }; done; sleep 2; for lbl in vdpsw2bp1 vdpsw2bp2; do o=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | awk -v L="$lbl" '$2==L{print $1; exit}'); [ -n "$o" ] || continue; if [ -e "/sys/bus/fsl-mc/devices/$o/driver" ]; then echo "$o" > "/sys/bus/fsl-mc/devices/$o/driver/unbind"; fi; restool dprc assign dprc.1 --object="$o" --plugged=0 || { echo "FAIL: unplug refused for $o ($lbl)" >&2; exit 1; }; restool dpbp destroy "$o" || { echo "FAIL: destroy refused for $o ($lbl)" >&2; exit 1; }; done; for lbl in vdpsw2mcp1 vdpsw2mcp2; do o=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | awk -v L="$lbl" '$2==L{print $1; exit}'); [ -n "$o" ] || continue; if [ -e "/sys/bus/fsl-mc/devices/$o/driver" ]; then echo "$o" > "/sys/bus/fsl-mc/devices/$o/driver/unbind"; fi; restool dprc assign dprc.1 --object="$o" --plugged=0 || { echo "FAIL: unplug refused for $o ($lbl)" >&2; exit 1; }; restool dpmcp destroy "$o" || { echo "FAIL: destroy refused for $o ($lbl)" >&2; exit 1; }; done; sleep 2; c=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | awk '$2=="vdpsw2"{print $1; exit}'); if [ -n "$c" ]; then restool dprc destroy "$c" || { echo "FAIL: destroy refused for scratch child $c" >&2; exit 1; }; fi; sleep 2; survivors=$(restool dprc show dprc.1 | grep vdpsw2 || true); if [ -n "$survivors" ]; then echo "FAIL: vdpsw2 labels survive teardown:" >&2; echo "$survivors" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "teardown done + verified: no vdpsw2 label survives in dprc.1"
steps.expect: zero exit; teardown is judged, not best-effort (rev 2, bead dpaa2-controlplane-dbf.18, after V-DPSW-2-run1 left all four companions plugged at root under a swallowed refusal). Each object is resolved by its vdpsw2* label; for EVERY driver-bound object — the dpsws AND the dpbp/dpmcp companions the fsl_mc_allocator binds — the allocator unbind (sysfs driver/unbind) precedes the unplug, because restool's client guard refuses to unplug a driver-bound object (the established V-LIFE-DPIO-1 law); a swallowed refusal was exactly the run1 leak. Unplug and destroy run loud: a refusal names the object and fails the step — refusals are findings, not noise. The scratch child is destroyed last and the eviction law releases its create-visible dpsw with it (ADR-0007 §3). dpsw destroy's exit status can be overwritten by dprc_close in a child (docs/baseline/dpsw.md silent-failure notes), so the closing verification pass — re-read dprc.1 and fail on any surviving vdpsw2 label — is the real evidence of removal, never a single exit code (DPSW-I7). Spaced destroys (sleep) keep clear of the ADR-0008 rescan race.

steps.label: capture root container post-probe (machine-checked zero deltas vs the step-0 banked census)
steps.expect: zero exit; the fresh root census is machine-diffed against the step-0 banked reference /run/vdpsw2-pre.census — diff exits non-zero and prints the delta on any mismatch, failing the step, so the zero-delta claim is now checked by the machine rather than asserted in prose (rev 2, bead dpaa2-controlplane-dbf.18). Every created object and the scratch child must be gone, no residue (self-cleaning plan); a survivor fails the step here instead of being read by eye (DPSW-I7). The diff is verbatim against the full listing, so any dpio/dpmcp pool residue the ADR-0011 one-portal-per-cycle shape leaves also surfaces as a delta (previously recorded, not gated); /run is tmpfs so a reboot clears both the residue and the banked reference.
